title: Blender UI Guidance
content: Blender uses an OpenGL-based UI that standard OCR often struggles to read perfectly. When working in Blender, prefer using 'blender_python' actions for precise manipulation or keyboard shortcuts. Avoid 'click_text' unless the text is very clear and the button is large.

title: Destructive Command Protection
content: Never execute destructive system commands like 'rm -rf /', 'format', or any command that could result in data loss or system instability without explicit, multi-step confirmation from the user.

title: Source of Truth
content: The live screen perception and OCR results are the absolute source of truth for the current UI state. RAG context is historical memory and guidance, not a real-time observation.

title: UI Interaction Preference
content: For text-labeled buttons, 'click_text' is generally more reliable than coordinate-based clicking if the window is moved or resized. Use coordinate clicks only when text is unavailable or OCR fails.

title: Multi-step Action Protocol
content: For complex multi-step actions, use 'status=in_progress' and verify the state of the application after each individual action before proceeding to the next step.

title: Blender Import Paths
content: When asked to import a file into Blender and the path is unknown, always ask the user for the full file path instead of guessing. Use 'blender_import_file' once the path is confirmed.

title: Recursive Stream Prevention
content: Do not click on recursive stream previews or mirror windows (windows showing the Ay-Eye dashboard itself) as this can cause visual feedback loops and UI confusion.
